convention: A door swing is drafted as an arc about the hinge whose radius is the leaf width; a double door or bi-fold bank draws one arc per LEAF, so expected_count is one per drawn leaf, not one per doorway. Read off these sheets themselves (bi-fold banks on Landscaping p7/p14/p15 draw two 45-deg arcs per fold meeting at a cusp; double doors on p15/p20 draw two mirrored arcs meeting mid-opening), not from an industry prior.
truth_rule: (a) arc on a DOOR-named layer, or (b) DOOR-named geometry within 2.0 pt of the fitted hinge; either way the unit must be genuinely drawn round a circle: arc-length ratio 0.90-1.20 (genuine swings measure 0.931-1.000 across the corpus; A-DOOR slab rectangles fit degenerately at <= 0.870) and sweep 20-200 deg, radius in the door band (1.25-6 ft at the detected scale).
layer_coverage: 160600/161063 units on this page carry a CAD layer name (99.7%)
notes: Coordinates are display-space pt from the RAW stroke extraction. detect_page runs build_chains before door_swings and build_chains welds unit endpoints in place, so live-engine centres can sit a fraction of a pt away and coincident twin arcs merge. Match detections to these arcs with a tolerance (4 pt on centre and radius), never by equality. What this truth CANNOT see: doors the drafter did not put on a DOOR-named layer and did not give a DOOR-layer jamb (none known on these pages), and pages with no layer metadata at all (see VERIFY.md for the list).
